markdown_content: ## Trace Graphic Feature Overview in Clo This section explains the "Trace as Internal Shape" feature in Clo, a 3D garment visualization software. It covers how to access this tool, what internal shapes are, and their initial visualization in the 3D window and pattern editor. The "Trace as Internal Shape" tool is accessed via the Edit Graphic Tool by right-clicking on a selected graphic in Clo. This feature creates an internal shape outline of the graphic within the 3D window, visible as a red shape in the pattern editor. This internal shape represents the graphic's contour and serves as a foundation for advanced graphic manipulation. --- ## Creating and Manipulating Internal Shapes This section details the process of cloning internal lines, converting shapes to holes, sewing pattern pieces, and superimposing elements to create complex graphic details. After tracing the internal shape, you can select internal lines and clone them as patterns with sewing, which duplicates the graphic elements as editable pattern pieces. Copying and pasting these pieces allows conversion to holes within the pattern, enabling cutouts or indentations in the garment design. Sewing the pieces together ensures proper garment construction and simulation. Using the "Superimpose Over" function layers these details realistically on top of the base garment, enhancing visual complexity. --- ## Customizing Graphic Properties and Effects This section explores various customization options for traced internal shapes, including color changes, material properties, indentation effects, and stitching details. Once pattern pieces are created from the internal shapes, you can assign any color or fabric type, such as shiny or velvet materials. It is possible to cut and sew pieces to integrate them fully into the garment, allowing them to sit below or be indented into the base fabric. Adjusting the thickness of the rendering can simulate indentation depth, making the graphic appear pressed into the surface. Additional effects like adding pressure to simulate pushing in the fabric or topstitching can enhance realism and design complexity. --- ## Using Internal Shapes with Different Backgrounds This section explains how Clo handles tracing graphics with different background colors and the implications for internal shape creation. When importing graphics with transparent PNG backgrounds, the tracing functions perfectly. For graphics with white backgrounds, Clo automatically ignores the white areas, recognizing them as background and excluding them from the trace. However, if the background is any other color (e.g., pink or purple), Clo traces the entire graphic including the background color. This behavior is specific to white backgrounds only, enabling more accurate tracing of patches or logos with white backgrounds. --- ## Aligning Graphics Using Internal Shapes for Production This section describes using internal shapes to precisely align graphics on garments, especially useful for repeating prints or production consistency. By tracing internal shapes of single graphics placed on garments, you can create reference shapes that align perfectly with all-over prints or patterned layouts. After tracing and deleting the original graphics, these internal shapes serve as guides in the print layout view, ensuring that graphics like logos or anchors are always centered or positioned consistently on every garment. This method accelerates workflow and improves alignment accuracy in production processes. --- ## Summary of Workflow for Using Trace as Internal Shape in Clo This final section summarizes the core steps for using the Trace as Internal Shape feature effectively. 1. Open the Edit Graphic Tool and select your graphic. 2. Right-click and choose "Trace as Internal Shape" to create the internal outline. 3. Use cloned internal lines to create new pattern pieces with sewing. 4. Convert necessary shapes to holes for cutouts or indentation effects. 5. Sew pieces together and use "Superimpose Over" to layer details. 6. Customize colors, materials, thickness, pressure effects, and stitching. 7. Account for background color behavior when importing graphics. 8. Use internal shapes as alignment guides in print layouts for consistent placement. This technique unlocks a wide range of graphic customization, enhanced realism, and production alignment capabilities within Clo. --- *Note: For further questions or advanced techniques, Clo’s YouTube channel and community forums provide additional resources and 3D designer support.*
